title: AWS Open-Sources Emulator for Local Testing of 200+ Services by Coding Agents
gist: AWS open-sourced (CC0) AWS Emulator, a Rust local HTTPS endpoint emulating public APIs of 200+ AWS services generated from 400+ Smithy models and written and tested by AI agents, aimed at coding agents iterating without cloud charges; fidelity varies (S3/DynamoDB/SQS ~2 in 3 tests pass, CloudFormation under 1 in 5) and it does not evaluate IAM.

insights.claim: AWS released AWS Emulator, a free local program serving an HTTPS endpoint for the public APIs of more than 200 AWS services, letting developers and coding agents create resources and hit real AWS errors without provisioning cloud resources or incurring charges.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Directly competes with LocalStack's commercial business; an official free emulator compresses the market for third-party AWS emulation.

insights.claim: AWS Emulator works by pointing the AWS CLI or SDKs at it via AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, ships as RPM/Debian packages for Linux, offers an embedded mode for Rust tests, and includes an aws-emulator skill to start it for coding agents.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Agent 'skills' are becoming a first-class distribution channel for developer tools.

insights.claim: AWS Emulator is written in Rust and generated from more than 400 Smithy API models, and AWS says agents wrote and tested the code across three agent teams: fidelity-test writers verified against real AWS, test replayers filing issues, and fixers, gated by compilation, standards, security and regression checks.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: A hyperscaler shipping a 200-service product built by agent teams is evidence that spec-plus-test-oracle tasks are now automatable at scale.
insights.locator: AWS says agents wrote and tested the code

insights.claim: The agent-driven development of AWS Emulator runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime Instances, AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeCommit.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: AWS is dogfooding AgentCore as an agent-workforce platform, a showcase for selling it to enterprises.
insights.locator: The work runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

insights.claim: AWS publishes versioned per-service fidelity scores, with a test passing only if status codes, side effects and exact errors match AWS; fidelity is best on control-plane APIs, while data-plane behavior and CloudFormation, Terraform and CDK support vary.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Published fidelity scores make emulator quality measurable, raising the bar for competitors.
insights.locator: How closely the emulator matches AWS varies

insights.claim: A developer counting AWS Emulator's published fidelity tests found S3, DynamoDB and SQS pass about 2 in 3, while CloudFormation passes under 1 in 5.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Infrastructure-as-code testing remains LocalStack's defensible niche for now.
insights.quote: S3, DynamoDB and SQS pass about 2 in 3. CloudFormation passes under 1 in 5.

insights.claim: AWS Emulator does not evaluate IAM or resource-based policies and must not be used for security testing; it also supports one shared account and Region per process, keeps state only in memory, and is unsuited for load or long-running tests.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Permission testing and IaC pipelines remain gaps where incumbent emulators retain value.

insights.claim: Compared with LocalStack, Floci and moto, AWS Emulator is generated from AWS's own API models, ships official fidelity scores and is public domain (CC0 1.0), but is not a drop-in replacement for permission testing or infrastructure-as-code pipelines.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Pressure on LocalStack's pricing and growth; watch whether AWS closes the IAM/IaC gaps quickly given agent-driven development speed.
insights.locator: Developers already have several local AWS stand-ins

insights.claim: AWS did not publish a prebuilt Docker image or GitHub Action for AWS Emulator, so community member Yurii Serhiichuk published both to fill the packaging gap.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Community packaging is accelerating adoption, a sign of developer demand.
